Docs/Replay/Guide

Replay

Escape menu and tally

2 min readOdin × GodotPage source ↓

The menu and tally are separate authored scenes using the original steel theme. The Escape menu dims the whole local view, centers horizontally and scrolls at smaller window heights. It keeps the existing save, spray, invite and settings controls and adds Quit. Quit first unloads the game and closes its session. Native builds allow a brief cleanup interval and then exit; browser builds display a closed-yard screen and leave the tab open.

Menu input does not move, dash, shoot, cast, ping or buy. The simulation and networking continue. Resume gets keyboard focus when the menu opens, and closing it consumes that frame's input so Enter does not also focus chat or a click fire a shot. Physical held-key state is retained while pending button presses are discarded, so holding Shift through Resume does not create a fresh dash. Tab opens the centered tally and releases unrelated gameplay UI focus. Releasing Tab still closes the tally while chat has focus.

The tally reads confirmed gameplay counters for connected players: kills, damage, healing credit (Mends), scrap and cores, plus the original registered Deaths column and application round-trip time (Ping ms). Observers do not acquire player rows. The original registers deaths but never credits player downs as deaths; that column remains zero here too. Telemetry is session metadata from the current authority, with zero for its local seat and -- until a peer has a fresh sample. The telemetry component measures application queues/pump time as well as transit. It is independent of the gameplay world, actions, events and checkpoints. The menu/tally assessment used content 45; adding telemetry did not change that gameplay contract. See the save guide for current content and conversion.

Shell
nix develop --command bash examples/replay_scrapyard/menu_run.sh
RSY_HEADED_HOST=1 RSY_AUDIO_DRIVER=Dummy RSY_MENU_QUIT=1 \
  RSY_MENU_CAPTURE=/absolute/existing/directory \
  nix develop --command bash examples/replay_scrapyard/menu_run.sh
RSY_ARMORY=mend nix develop --command bash examples/replay_scrapyard/combat_run.sh

The browser UI gate exercises the same menu, resizing, tally/chat focus and peer departure, alongside the earlier UI and ordnance checks. Evidence records the native/browser results and a communications-adapter regression found during this work. A gameplay resync preserves chat on the still-admitted connection; fencing, failed admission and new connection/epoch boundaries retain their guards.

Broader actor presentation parity, additional platform and browser tests, hardware listening, playtests and full M9 comparisons remain requirements.
